title: Evaluation metrics and the accuracy trap

videos.script: The lapse model is right about eighty-six percent of members. That sounds like a model worth having. {{eightysix}} A model that knows nothing at all is right about eighty-three percent. It says nobody lapses, and most members do not. {{nothing}} Three points of difference, and the number everybody quotes cannot see them. That is the accuracy trap. {{trap}} So this lesson takes the answers apart. Four kinds: the ones caught, the ones missed, the false alarms, and the rest. {{four}} From those come precision and recall. And a threshold, which is a business decision dressed as a number. {{threshold}} With a voucher at ten reais, the best place to cut is not point five. It is nearer point two. {{cut}} Then the scores that judge a ranking instead of a cut. And a check that a probability means what it says. {{ranking}} Last, the same questions for an amount instead of a yes or no. {{amount}} By the end, you will know which number to log. And which to put in front of the person who asked for the model. {{end}}
